source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company states it hedges roughly 80% of its forex exposure
inr_exposure.evidence: CFO Nitin Agrawal stated on an FY25/FY26 earnings call that Alkem hedges approximately 80% of its ForEx exposure as part of risk management given growing international operations; not independently confirmed from AR MD&A text (source was earnings-call commentary, not the primary annual report).

pli_scheme.evidence: No disclosure found confirming Alkem as a named beneficiary of India's PLI scheme for APIs/KSMs/Drug Intermediates (47-48 approved applicants industry-wide) or the broader pharma PLI scheme (~55 selected firms); Alkem was not identified in available sources among the named beneficiary lists.

china_plus_one.evidence: AR/press materials note global pharma industry context of companies 'increasingly diversifying supply chains and investing in regional manufacturing capabilities'; Sun Pharma frames its Emerging Markets and RoW businesses as diversification away from single-geography dependence, but no explicit 'China+1' framing or direct revenue attribution to China-sourcing diversification was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Sun Pharma discloses foreign currency transaction gains/losses as part of EBITDA reconciliation in results, implying active FX management, but specific hedging ratio/policy text was not accessible in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharma is named among ~55 companies selected by the Indian government under the Rs 15,000 crore PLI scheme for the pharmaceutical sector (covering complex generics, APIs/KSMs, and other drug categories), alongside Dr. Reddy's and Cipla; specific revenue or incentive quantum attributable to Sun Pharma not disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Search-derived summaries describe Shyam Metalics as predominantly a domestic-demand story (exports ~10% of sales, providing 'cushion against domestic demand cycles'). No China+1 / supply-chain diversification framing was found; growth narrative is centered on India's infrastructure pipeline and institutional/government contractor demand, not export diversification.

govt_capex.evidence: Third-party commentary links Shyam Metalics' TMT/long-products capacity growth to India's ~Rs 11 lakh crore National Infrastructure Pipeline (roads, railways, real estate), citing institutional sales at roughly 18% of order book (as of late 2025, not confirmed as a direct FY25 AR disclosure). No explicit revenue_pct tied to government capex was found in a verifiable primary-source form.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Described as carrying a light balance sheet: gross debt of roughly Rs 957 crore, gross debt-to-equity ~0.08x, net debt-to-EBITDA ~ -0.16x (net cash position) per third-party financial trackers. No specific floating-vs-fixed rate split was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Coking coal and iron ore cited as key cost inputs with 'elevated' and margin-squeezing prices; company has backward integration (captive power meeting ~80% of electricity needs, a 3.6 MTPA pellet plant, in-house sponge iron/ferroalloys) to partially insulate margins. No explicit raw-material-cost-as-%-of-revenue figure was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Given exports are only ~10% of revenue, USD/forex exposure appears limited; no hedging policy disclosure was found via search.

pli_scheme.evidence: Shyam Metalics' Flat Products arm was selected as a qualifier/most competitive bidder under the Government of India's PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel (covering products like high-strength auto-grade steel and CRGO electrical steel), per Business Standard/Steel Ministry reporting. Revenue contribution from PLI-linked products not disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Usha Martin has genuine, sizeable export/international revenue (third-party sources cite figures ranging 30%-55% of revenue depending on whether 'direct exports from India' or 'total international revenue incl. UK/Dubai/Thailand subsidiaries' is meant) into oil & gas, mining, elevators, cranes and infrastructure end-markets across US/UK/Europe/Middle East/SE Asia. No explicit China+1 or supply-chain-diversification-from-China framing was found in available sources — narrative is about global market leadership and end-market diversification, not China displacement.

govt_capex.evidence: Wire ropes are sold into infrastructure/construction end-uses (bridges, flyovers, metro rail) domestically, but no specific government-capex-linked revenue percentage was disclosed in sources reviewed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Multiple sources describe Usha Martin as having significantly reduced debt and being 'almost debt free' (cash flow release of ~Rs 141 crore cited in FY25 commentary), but no floating-vs-fixed rate breakdown was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is steel wire rod (internally sourced/backward integrated at the Ranchi/Jamshedpur-linked value chain); no explicit iron-ore/coking-coal/crude-linked raw-material-cost-as-%-of-revenue figure was found for Usha Martin specifically.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export/international revenue (30-55% per differing third-party figures) is largely USD/GBP-denominated given manufacturing and sales subsidiaries in the US, UK, Dubai, Thailand and Singapore; sources note forex gains have bolstered income, but no specific hedging policy or USD-revenue percentage was confirmed from a primary disclosure.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company/media commentary tied to Lupin's FY25 reporting states: 'Policies like the proposed Biosecure Act in the U.S., aimed at reducing dependency on China, are prompting global pharma players to diversify suppliers... Lupin, with its robust India-based manufacturing and CDMO operations, is well placed to support this transition.' Also: 'FY25 was a transformational year for Lupin Manufacturing Solutions (LMS)... reflected strong alignment with global industry trends such as supply chain diversification, CDMO outsourcing, and high-potency APIs.' This is strategic/positioning language rather than an explicit quantified revenue attribution to China+1, hence rated moderate rather than strong.

rural.evidence: Lupin Foundation's 'Lives Program' (CSR, not commercial revenue) serves 1,785+ villages across eight states in FY25 (Rajasthan-Alwar, Maharashtra-Palghar mobile medical units); this is a rural CSR/healthcare-access initiative, not a disclosed rural revenue percentage.

govt_capex.evidence: Commentary notes Lupin's 'tender business, particularly in India's institutional business segment, has shown meaningful growth and is expected to continue at steady levels' — qualitative only, no percentage of revenue disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedges plus forex derivatives (layered hedging strategy); no forward-contract notional or hedge-ratio percentage found
inr_exposure.evidence: 'Lupin operates in 100+ markets and is exposed to currency fluctuations, particularly those of USD-INR, EUR-INR, and ZAR-INR. While natural hedges and forex derivatives are deployed, extreme currency movements can impact profitability. Lupin's treasury operations actively monitor exposures and adopt layered hedging strategies.'

pli_scheme.evidence: Multiple sources indicate Lupin committed to invest approximately ₹1,000 crore leveraging India's PLI incentives to expand manufacturing capacity for high-value generics/APIs, reducing import reliance; framed together with Lupin's API Plus/CDMO (Lupin Manufacturing Solutions) growth strategy. No specific PLI-linked revenue percentage disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Glenmark's API subsidiary, Glenmark Life Sciences (GLS) — the entity historically associated with the China+1/API-diversification narrative — was divested: Nirma Limited completed acquisition of a 75% stake from Glenmark Pharmaceuticals in March 2024, reducing Glenmark's residual holding to ~7.84%, making GLS no longer a subsidiary. Glenmark Pharma continues to source certain APIs from GLS under a 5-year supply arrangement starting FY2024-25, but recent reporting does not frame this as a China+1 diversification growth driver for the consolidated parent.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt reported at ~₹489 crore as of March 2025 (company has trended toward being net-cash positive following the FY24 GLS stake sale proceeds used for debt repayment); no floating-rate liability percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Relies primarily on natural hedging rather than extensive use of derivative/forward-contract instruments
inr_exposure.evidence: Per Glenmark Global CFO commentary: the company relies on natural hedging for currency exposure rather than extensively using derivative instruments like forward contracts. No formal hedge-ratio or USD-revenue percentage found.

pli_scheme.evidence: General industry reporting names pharma broadly as a major recipient of India's PLI scheme investment (~₹1.06 trillion across 14 sectors), but no source specifically confirmed Glenmark Pharmaceuticals (post-GLS-divestiture, standalone/consolidated parent) as a named PLI beneficiary; the API-linked PLI angle was more associated with the now-divested Glenmark Life Sciences entity.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Third-party financial trackers describe Ajanta Pharma as near debt-free/net-cash (net debt reported negative as of Mar-2025), implying minimal floating-rate liability exposure, but no explicit AR disclosure of floating-rate debt % was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export markets contributed ~69% of FY25 revenue (branded generics across India/Asia/Africa plus US generics), implying material foreign-currency revenue exposure, but no explicit USD-specific % or hedging policy detail was found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No source found naming Ajanta Pharma as a PLI (Production Linked Incentive) scheme beneficiary; company operates one API facility for captive/in-house consumption rather than as a KSM/API PLI-scheme participant.

china_plus_one.evidence: General industry commentary (not company-specific AR text) notes Indian CDMOs broadly, including JB Pharma's CDMO segment, are seen as beneficiaries of the global 'China+1' supply-chain diversification trend, but no direct quote from JB Pharma's own MD&A attributing growth to China+1 was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: International business (Russia, South Africa, CDMO, API) was ~42% of FY25 revenue (₹1,649cr of ₹3,918cr total), implying meaningful foreign-currency exposure, but no explicit USD-revenue % or hedging policy was found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No source found naming JB Chemicals/JB Pharma as a PLI scheme beneficiary. Company's API facility at Panoli (Gujarat) passed a 2025 USFDA inspection with zero observations, but PLI participation was not confirmed; API segment revenue is small (~₹19-86cr) and reportedly declining.

rural.evidence: AR references rural healthcare outreach (e.g., multi-purpose satellite centers started at Waghai and Chhappi, Gujarat, with more planned at Radhanpur, Naswadi and Dediapada) but this reads as CSR/access initiative, not a disclosed rural revenue segment.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company has multi-currency exposure via branded generics operations in Brazil (BRL), Germany (EUR), US (USD) and other markets; no explicit USD-revenue percentage or hedging policy disclosure found in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Torrent Pharmaceuticals Limited is listed as a qualified beneficiary under Group A (global manufacturing revenue ≥ ₹5,000 crore) of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (55 companies qualified nationally; ₹15,000 crore outlay over six years).

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/earnings commentary describes Divi's as positioning itself as 'the primary beneficiary of the China+1 strategy in the CDMO space,' with management citing raw-material sourcing diversification away from China and custom-synthesis vertical growth tied to customers reducing China dependence; multi-site API/intermediate capacity marketed as supply-security for regulated-market (US/EU/Japan) customers. Note: this is drawn from earnings-call/analyst summaries, not verified against the AR's verbatim MD&A text.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is effectively debt-free with negative net debt (~₹7,427 crore net cash as of March 2025), suggesting minimal floating-rate liability exposure, though no explicit floating-rate disclosure was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Sources mention solvent recovery systems, backward integration and diversified raw-material sourcing that reduce input costs and stabilize raw material prices; no disclosed raw-material-cost-as-%-of-revenue figure or explicit petrochemical/crude linkage found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports account for ~90% of revenue with Europe and the US together contributing ~74%, implying high foreign-currency (largely USD/EUR) revenue exposure; explicit USD-denominated revenue percentage and hedging policy not found in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories Limited is named among the 55 companies qualified under India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (Department of Pharmaceuticals, Nov 2021 announcement), under Category 2 covering APIs/KSMs/Drug Intermediates not covered by the earlier bulk-drug PLI scheme.

rural.evidence: CMD (Suresh Narayanan/Manish Tiwary) commentary describes rural India as 'one of the most significant growth opportunities,' with the company deepening its 2019-launched 'RUrban' (rural+urban) strategy, present in ~208,500 villages, calibrating assortment/pack-price architecture and route-to-market for rural penetration; rural recovery in FY24-25 was aided by monsoon outcomes, farm income and government support even as urban consumption moderated (overall FY24-25 revenue grew only 1.7% YoY). No explicit rural revenue % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company commentary notes rising raw material costs and crude-linked packaging expenses pressuring margins; despite sourcing over 97% of materials locally, management states it is 'not fully insulated' from global cost inflation. No specific raw-material-as-%-of-revenue figure disclosed in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: ~97%+ of raw materials sourced locally, implying only a small residual (coffee/cocoa-type) import exposure; FY25 foreign exchange earnings from exports were reported around Rs 785 crore against forex outgo of ~Rs 3,735 crore, but no explicit hedging policy or USD revenue % was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Nestlé India received government approval under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for processed fruits & vegetables (approved Dec 2021, part of the food-processing PLI cohort alongside ITC, Britannia, Parle) explicitly to boost exports; no separate revenue/PLI-linked contribution % disclosed.

rural.evidence: Commentary notes price sensitivity is higher among rural and urban mass-market consumers, with large players competing on pricing and retail reach; distribution spans 100,000+ retail outlets and 10,000+ on-premise locations nationally. No rural-specific revenue % disclosed; growth narrative centers more on premiumization (Prestige & Above) than rural/urban split.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt reported at ~Rs 868 crore as of Mar-25 (up from ~Rs 749 crore Mar-24), short-term borrowings ~Rs 693 crore, CARE AA rated; company confirmed not classified as a SEBI 'Large Corporate.' No floating-vs-fixed rate split disclosed in available sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: FY24 saw volatile grain, ENA (extra neutral alcohol) and glass costs pressuring gross margins; premiumization mix-shift and price hikes offset the pressure. FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 13.8% (from 12.3% in FY24) aided by a more stable raw-material environment, and management expects softening grain/ENA prices into FY26. Company commissioned a 350 KLPD distillery at Sitapur for backward integration into ENA supply. No raw-material-as-%-of-revenue figure disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports to 100+ countries (incl. US, Canada, Europe, SE Asia, 35+ travel-retail locations), reported at roughly 8% of total revenue in FY2022-23 (most recent disclosed figure found; not confirmed for FY24-25). Commentary notes INR depreciation vs. major currencies could affect international margins, but no explicit hedging policy was found.

rural.evidence: Search-sourced business updates indicate Phoenix Mills expanded into Tier-2 cities (Phoenix Palassio, Lucknow and Phoenix Citadel, Indore), with malls achieving ~94% average trading occupancy within 6-8 quarters of launch; company plans to grow retail portfolio to over 14 million sq ft by 2027 and 18 million sq ft by 2030, including further Tier-2 presence. This is Tier-2 urban expansion, not rural, and no rural revenue % is disclosed in any source found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Third-party summaries reference Phoenix Mills' gross debt (~Rs.3,953 crore per an older snapshot) and cost of borrowing (~8.4%), but no primary-source AR/MD&A disclosure of floating vs. fixed rate debt composition could be accessed (all direct AR/IR/broker-report fetches returned HTTP 403).

inr_exposure.evidence: No foreign-currency revenue, debt, or international operations found in any source; Phoenix Mills' mall/office/residential portfolio and expansion pipeline (Mumbai, Bengaluru, Pune, Chennai, Lucknow, Indore, Kolkata, Gujarat, Thane, Coimbatore, Chandigarh) is entirely India-based.

rural.evidence: MD&A macro-economic outlook section notes 'private consumption is likely to gain steam with a pick-up in rural activity' as a general economic tailwind for FY2024-25 outlook, but this is sector/macro commentary, not a disclosed company revenue split.

govt_capex.evidence: MD&A cites Government of India Ministry of Tourism schemes (Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD, UDAN, Dekho Apna Desh) promoting tourism infrastructure/destinations, and references 'the government's thrust on capex' as a macro GDP driver, as sector tailwinds. No revenue_pct tied to government contracts disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Note 19/40 (Consolidated FY2023-24): Total Borrowings were Rs.260.49 crores as at March 31, 2024, of which Rs.209.63 crores (~80.5%) was a secured term loan from banks at variable/floating rate (SONIA + margin, related to overseas subsidiary St James Court Hotel Ltd, London). 'The total borrowing at variable rate was Rs.209.63 crores as at March 31, 2024 (March 31, 2023 - Rs.314.91 crores).'

crude_exposure.evidence: Corporate Governance Report explicitly states: 'The Company does not deal in commodities and hence the disclosure pursuant to the SEBI Circular dated November 15, 2018 is not required to be given.'

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Group uses forward exchange contracts, interest rate swaps, currency swaps and options to hedge foreign currency and interest rate exposure; however, 'there are no such instruments outstanding as at Balance sheet date' (unhedged as of March 31, 2024). Net derivative exposures are kept within Board-approved limits.
inr_exposure.evidence: Foreign currency debt includes a GBP loan (St James Court Hotel Ltd, London, £20m outstanding, SONIA+2.5%) and a USD loan (United Overseas Holdings Inc., $6.04m outstanding, 4.5%). Revenue from USA operations was Rs.661.00cr (9.8% of total) and UK Rs.543.36cr (8.0%) out of total group revenue of Rs.6,768.75cr.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/industry commentary (not confirmed as verbatim AR text) notes Kajaria is expanding footprint in Middle East/Europe export markets, and that anti-dumping duties on Chinese tiles by various countries opened an export window for Indian tile manufacturers generally (a sector-wide 'China+1' sourcing narrative). India's tile exports fell from ~INR 200bn (FY24) to ~INR 160bn (FY25) due to Red Sea disruptions/freight costs and geopolitical tensions, suggesting Kajaria's own export momentum, if any, was muted in FY25. No verbatim AR quote was directly confirmed since the primary PDF could not be fetched.

rural.evidence: Company/industry commentary repeatedly cites Kajaria's 'widest reach in Tier 2/3 markets' and distribution network growth (from ~900 dealers in FY14 to ~1,500+ currently) driven by rural/semi-urban penetration; pent-up retail demand from tier II/III cities cited as a revenue driver in recent years. No explicit rural revenue % disclosed in sources found.

govt_capex.evidence: Secondary sources cite real estate upcycle (residential, Tier I/II cities), government housing scheme 'Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana', and infrastructure spend (airports, railway stations, Gati Shakti national master plan ~US$1.3 trillion) as demand drivers for tiles, with tiles described as a 'last leg proxy' to construction activity. No explicit revenue_pct tied to government/infra work was disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Natural gas/fuel (along with pet coke) is repeatedly cited as a major energy input for kiln operations, energy-intensive manufacturing. Secondary analyst commentary (not confirmed against primary AR text) suggested gas/fuel costs at times approached ~20-30% of cost of production/revenue, and cited sharp regional gas price spikes (e.g., Morbi gas cost rising from ~Rs47-48 to ~Rs84.5/SCM) forcing industry-wide price hikes of 12-40%. Could not confirm an exact AR-disclosed raw-material percentage.

inr_exposure.evidence: No revenue-side USD/FX exposure disclosure found; Kajaria is predominantly a domestic-revenue business with modest, declining export volumes in FY25 amid Red Sea/freight disruptions.

pli_scheme.evidence: No mention found of Kajaria being a PLI scheme beneficiary; PLI schemes found in searches relate to electronics, pharma, telecom, auto sectors, not ceramics/tiles.

china_plus_one.evidence: Titan's international business (Tanishq/Mia jewellery stores in North America and GCC — 23 stores total as of FY25: 21 Tanishq + 2 Mia) is described as an expansion initiative, not framed around China+1/supply-chain diversification. Notably, for eyewear, roughly 65% of products are reportedly imported from China, Korea and Taiwan (35% manufactured in India) — i.e., Titan is a net importer from China in that sub-segment, not a China+1 beneficiary. No diversification-from-China export narrative found.

rural.evidence: FY25/FY26 commentary (via press coverage of AR MD&A) cites 'a growing middle India from Tier-II, Tier-III and Tier-IV towns' as a structural demand driver alongside rising discretionary spending and category formalisation. No explicit rural/tier-town revenue percentage disclosed in sources found.

govt_capex.evidence: No government capex/infrastructure-linked demand narrative found for Titan (consumer discretionary jewellery/watches/eyewear business, not construction-linked).

crude_exposure.evidence: No direct crude-oil/energy raw-material exposure found; Titan's key input is gold/diamonds (precious metals), not crude/energy. Not a relevant signal per company's actual disclosed cost structure.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Reported (via CFO commentary in press coverage, not confirmed verbatim AR text) that Titan follows a near-100% gold hedging strategy for import cost exposure, with ~120-day supply/price visibility via advance procurement contracts.
inr_exposure.evidence: This hedging relates to gold IMPORT COST exposure (raw material side), not USD-denominated revenue exposure. No revenue-side FX/export USD percentage was found, so usd_revenue_pct is left null per instructions.

pli_scheme.evidence: No mention found of Titan being a PLI scheme beneficiary; searches returned only generic PLI scheme sector info (electronics, pharma, telecom, auto, etc.), none referencing Titan/jewellery/watches/eyewear.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: No formal hedging percentage/policy disclosed in sources reviewed; company narrative cites a 'natural hedge'/currency arbitrage from USD-denominated revenue against an INR cost base as a margin driver.
inr_exposure.evidence: IKS Health (Inventurus Knowledge Solutions) is a US healthcare BPO/tech-enablement provider; ~96% of FY25 revenue (Rs 2,664 crore total) came from the US market, with limited presence in Canada/Australia and India; company partners with 700+ clients covering ~18% of all US physicians. Revenue is earned in USD while a significant portion of costs are incurred in INR, cited as a source of margin benefit (FY25 EBITDA margin ~30%).

govt_capex.evidence: JSW Infrastructure (India's second-largest private port operator, 13 ports/terminals in India plus O&M terminals in UAE) frames its growth strategy around India's government-led port infrastructure push, including the Sagarmala Programme and PM Gati Shakti multimodal connectivity initiative; company is developing a Gati Shakti Multi-Modal cargo terminal near Chennai and is scaling total capacity toward 400 MTPA by FY30 with an estimated Rs 30,000 crore capex outlay (FY25-FY30, later revised to Rs 13,500-14,000 crore for FY26-28), directly tied to national port-capacity expansion goals. No explicit revenue % tagged to government-capex-linked cargo was found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company raised Rs 7,503 crore via QIP partly to fund debt reduction alongside brownfield/inorganic expansion, implying meaningful existing debt load, but no floating-vs-fixed rate breakdown was found in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: JSW Infrastructure's cargo mix includes coal (Ennore, Mangalore, Paradip coal terminals), iron ore (Paradip, Jaigarh/Dharamtar/Southwest), containers, and liquid cargo (465,000 cbm liquid tank storage facility in Fujairah, UAE), indicating some crude/liquid-linked exposure, but exact commodity-mix percentages were not confirmed from sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company has UAE operations (O&M terminals, liquid storage in Fujairah/Dibba) implying some foreign-currency exposure; press reports cite meaningful net foreign-exchange losses in a subsequent period (~Rs 363 crore FY26 vs Rs 88 crore prior year) that dented standalone profit, suggesting unhedged/partially hedged FX exposure (likely FC-denominated debt tied to UAE assets), but no USD revenue % or formal hedging policy was disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: MD&A: 'As global supply chains continue to diversify, our strong alignment with India's industrial growth becomes increasingly evident.' Also, under Technology Absorption: company innovating 'to eliminate/reduce the heavy rare earth magnets' and developing 'magnet free motor technologies' (developed magnets with Celerium to replace heavy rare earth elements) — reducing China-sourced rare-earth dependency in EV motors. rate_sensitive.evidence: As of 31 March 2025, the Company had nil current/variable-rate borrowings (all loans repaid during the year); variable rate borrowings were INR 2,330.59 million as of 31 March 2024. Interest rate sensitivity: 1% rate change impact on PAT was INR 8.72 million (FY25) vs INR 16.86 million (FY24).

crude_exposure.evidence: 'The Company consumes alloy steel, steel, aluminium and copper as some of the major commodities...
